# A Board window change scans 10,000 records three times for one column

## Context

The large Task Board example renders 110 cards from a column of 6,200. A single scroll-window change still walks the 10,000-record store three times. This surfaced in the operator’s planning-family debt audit.

## The Problem

With the existing big-data ticket store, set the New column's window start from 0 to 100. Counting calls to `getColumnRecords` and the store's hydration path gave the same result in two independent instrumented Node runs:

| Operation | Column reconciliations | Full population reads | Records visited by those reads |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Shift New's rendered window | 1 | 3 | 30,000 |
| Move one record from New to Triage | 2 | 6 | 60,000 |
| Change its title | 0 | 0 | 0 |

These are structural counts. A call to hydrate an already hydrated record does not allocate another record.

## The Architectural Reality

[`reconcileColumn`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/50fcfc526c/src/board/Container.mjs#L1455) obtains the sorted population before choosing the card window. Two selection-position reads then enter [`getCardPosition`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/50fcfc526c/src/board/Container.mjs#L703), which rebuilds that population from the store. A cross-column move can ask about the focused card in the destination while reconciling the source. Store membership and ordering remain authoritative.

## The Fix

Reuse the ordered population or resolved position while a single reconciliation is current. Preserve selection changes made through normal keyboard, filter and move operations. Measure each population requested so that one column's reused result can never supply another column's answer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic count over the 10,000-card fixture shows that selecting a new rendered window no longer repeats equivalent population reads for roving focus. The plain title-edit control keeps zero full reads.
- [ ] A move between columns produces the correct counts, WIP state, new/old positions, rendered order and keyboard focus. Include hidden records and retention across an offscreen round trip.
- [ ] Compare the before/after counts from the normal scroll/reconciliation entry point. Report browser timing separately if measured.

## Out of Scope

A new permanent store copy, a browser performance claim inferred from Node timings, and a rewrite of the scale example.

## Related

Scale example #21627. Multi-window planning #21915. Live latest-open + closed sweep: reviewed the newest 24 Engine issues and the all-state searches for getColumnRecords/window and roving/10,000. The shipped scale-example leaf owns the demonstration. The current column-summary feature operates on its existing population and does not own these repeated reads. MC Board-restoration and prior-art search added no existing owner.

Save this as `tmp/planning-audit/probe.mjs` in an Engine checkout with dependencies installed, then run `node tmp/planning-audit/probe.mjs`. It reads the shipped classes and holds the fixture inside one Node process. The numeric counters and VDOM fields are the primary observations.

```js
import {setup} from '../../test/playwright/setup.mjs';
import Neo from '../../src/Neo.mjs';
import '../../src/core/_export.mjs';
import '../../src/manager/Instance.mjs';
import Board from '../../src/board/Container.mjs';
import TicketStore from '../../examples/board/bigData/TicketStore.mjs';

const appName = 'BoardDebtProbe';
setup({neoConfig:{unitTestMode:true,allowVdomUpdatesInTests:false,useDomApiRenderer:false},
    appConfig:{name:appName,isMounted:()=>true,vnodeInitialising:false}});
const store = Neo.create(TicketStore), board = Neo.create(Board, {appName,store,columns:[
    {status:'new'}, {status:'triage'}, {status:'waiting'}, {status:'solved'}, {status:'closed'}
]});
let hydrated = 0, reads = 0, reconciles = 0, readDetails = [];
const hydrate = store.hydrateRecord.bind(store), getRecords = board.getColumnRecords.bind(board),
      reconcile = board.reconcileColumn.bind(board);
store.hydrateRecord = (...args) => { hydrated++; return hydrate(...args) };
board.getColumnRecords = (...args) => { reads++; const before = hydrated, caller = new Error().stack.split('\n')[2].trim(), result = getRecords(...args);
    readDetails.push({status:args[0], caller, populationHydrations:hydrated-before, returned:result.length}); return result };
board.reconcileColumn = (...args) => { reconciles++; return reconcile(...args) };
function measure(label, fn) {
    hydrated = reads = reconciles = 0; readDetails = [];
    const start = performance.now(); fn(); const ms = performance.now() - start;
    console.log(JSON.stringify({label, count:store.getCount(), hydrated, reads, reconciles, readDetails, ms:+ms.toFixed(3)}))
}
try {
    const column = board.getColumn('new'), record = store.get('t-1');
    console.log(JSON.stringify({newCount:column.count, rendered:column.body.items.length, sliced:column.isSliced}));
    measure('windowStart 0→100', () => column.setWindowStart(100));
    measure('title edit', () => {record.title = 'Changed title'});
    measure('status new→triage', () => {record.status = 'triage'});
} finally { board.destroy(); store.destroy() }
```
